Hydrogen bonds are strongest when the donor and acceptor atoms are close together and the bond is near-linear (180°), with the hydrogen pointing directly at the acceptor. They weaken with greater distance, bent geometry, and competing interactions that disrupt donor–acceptor alignment. The note about hydrogen ions from anaerobic glycolysis concerns H⁺ ions, not hydrogen bonds, so it does not apply here.
CONFIDENCE: 85
